gap: No result ChatGPT got states Wh per pound or dollars per Wh for the 12V 100Ah candidates; on those two derived figures the Redodo 12V 100Ah Group 24 Bluetooth ($0.203/Wh, 58.7 Wh/lb) and the Vatrer 12V 100Ah Group 24 150A ($0.203/Wh) both beat ChatGPT's value pick, the LiTime Group 24 Bluetooth ($0.243/Wh, 57.8 Wh/lb), and the LiTime Xtra-Mini is the Wh/lb leader at 66.9.
standout_why: BatteryTrail (cited, updated 2026-11-06) computes cost per cycle at 80% DoD ($0.056 LiTime, $0.200 Battle Born) and lists weights and prices, but never Wh/lb or $/Wh, and it covers no Redodo or Vatrer model. ExploringOffGrid (cited, 2026-10-31) has no weights or prices at all, so nothing can be derived from it. LiTime's own non-Bluetooth Group 24 page prints 60.95 Wh/lb for itself only. None of the pages puts the four sub-$320 Group 24 batteries on one $/Wh and Wh/lb line.
decides: ChatGPT's 'best overall value' is the LiTime Group 24 Bluetooth at $311.09. At the same 1,280 Wh, 100A-class BMS, Bluetooth, low-temp cutoff and 5-year warranty, the Redodo Group 24 Bluetooth costs $51 less ($0.203 vs $0.243 per Wh) and is 0.36 lb lighter, and the Vatrer Group 24 at the same $259.99 adds a 150A BMS (1,920 W continuous vs 1,280 W, i.e. 7.4 W per dollar vs 4.1). If weight is the shopper's number, the LiTime Xtra-Mini (19.13 lb, 66.9 Wh/lb) wins for $8 more than the Group 24 Bluetooth. Battle Born stays a 3x-the-price premium pick ($0.62/Wh, about 41 Wh/lb) whose only derived advantage is warranty length.
